$comment: THE asset library — single source of truth for the visual layer. One record flows to the Scene Director's vocabulary (packages/scene/src/catalog.ts), the renderer (apps/web fetches GET /assets/library), and the extractor (scripts/extract-assets.py produces the served PNG from each `from`). To ADD an asset: add a record (with a `from`), then `npm run assets:extract`. INTERIM library: CC0 Kenney 'Tiny' trio (Tiny Town, Tiny Dungeon) + Tiny Creatures (CC0) — all 16x16, mutually cohesive. Pixel Crawler kept under raw-packs/pixel-crawler for future cherry-picking. Swappable for a paid pack later with no contract change (tags are stable; only `art`/`from`/geometry move).

assets.desc: the great bronze bell — corroded, banded, big enough to seal a man inside
a standing iron lamp post, lit
a low stone weir combing the river into a white sill of foam
a heavy iron mooring ring bolted through a worn stone block
the great bell's iron clapper, torn loose and left to rust
a sealed tomb slab, iron-banded, its wax seal unbroken
a fishing net strung between posts to dry, weed still caught in it
a ship's anchor stood on its flukes, rope still bent to the ring
a weathered channel buoy riding low at the waterline
a village well — stone ring, crossbeam, and a waiting bucket
a rope ladder swaying against the trunk, rungs worn smooth
a fluted stone column holding up the dark
the column snapped at a man's height — rubble where the rest fell
a floor lever nobody remembers the purpose of
an iron grid gate, points hungry for the floor
hanging chains — one shackle empty, one broken
a pair of shackles, opened or slipped
a floor plate of spikes — two are already stained
a hexagonal pine coffin, nailed shut
the same coffin, lid ajar — someone is still home
a chalk-and-blood summoning circle, candles still warm
a cluster of cave crystals, lit from inside
a rough monolith whose rune pulses cold light
an upright iron case shaped like a person — it drips
a witch's cauldron at a slow green boil
a wooden table collapsed at one end, leg snapped to splinters
a chair tipped on its side, one leg gone
furniture under a dust sheet, waiting like a ghost
